assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the active_provisional KONOSUBA_KAREN_DONNELLY_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (twelve evidence-proportional sections) and the active_provisional KONOSUBA_KAREN_DONNELLY_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md (three unequal rules KD-R01 to KD-R03, no independent prediction result). Both concern the self-introduced head of the Donnelly family in the connected CONTEXP01 arc (census row 70): the earlier forest-house rescue at U019P454-P524 and the U021 episode of reception and contract, next-day monster work, a one-kill report and confrontation, a nighttime intrusion and the next-morning evidence handoff. The reported MASK adventurer Karen is not joined to this subject and nothing about her is used. Kazuma Satō narrates; Karen's affect is observed by him, and Darkness's and Megumin's accounts of her are testimony. The cohort evidence index, native provenance JSON and rule inventory the items link were read only as method context; they are not curated on this subject and no claim rests on them. Both items are labelled provisional, and every claim here inherits that label. No primary source was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The CONTEXP01 arc only: the earlier rescue in the Megumin episode (U019) and the later U021 episode placed after the Elroad journey and an interval (U021P4), ordered by paragraph. Register and stance change repeatedly within the U021 episode (formal welcome, rivalrous insult, recovered business smile, mockery, alarm, renewed authority, fear, renewed threat, retraction at P515-P517); these are within-arc states, not independent samples, and the closing frightened apology is not a developmental endpoint. No dates, development across time, or life outside the arc are evidenced. She is not shown to know of Kazuma's death when she mocks the one-kill report (P213 is interrupted).
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model names observed valued ends (commercial return, competitive standing, useful service, protection of the household position, immediate safety) and three conditional rules: useful cooperation receives courtesy while an active status rivalry recruits comparison (KD-R01); a profitable practice whose costs fall on others is defended through commercial legitimacy (KD-R02); defiance backed by believed protection reverses under immediate personal consequence and can recover (KD-R03). Each rule has support, contrary evidence, rivals, conditions and a falsifier. Not B: the items state that the global weights of her ends are not fixed and no ordering of money, safety, reputation and long-term success is established, so which motive decides a new choice is undetermined; generic hostile-noble convention and ordinary fear are unseparated rivals. Not D: the dedicated monograph and model give a located, conditioned interpretation rather than scattered observations.

Only the earlier rescue and the later episode, with rapid within-episode register changes; the monograph says the closing apology cannot serve as a developmental endpoint. Not D: there is no sequence of states over time, only one connected arc. Grade kept above NOT_ASSESSED because the chronology and its limit are themselves located.

Located written-Japanese observations tied to acts: カレンと申します (P28) for formal self-presentation, 従業員に代わり (P54) for an apology on an employee's behalf, deferential サトウ様 and elaborated praise to the valued hire beside cutting comparisons to Darkness, お金を生み出す (P476) for the money redefinition, and the P515 legal-status assertion and bounty threat retracted in the same turn; the model directs varying the act rather than repeating a catchphrase. Not C: a handful of forms, no counts and no register system beyond the hire-rival contrast. Not E: forms are tied to acts and recipients rather than listed.

Formal receptions, tea and snacks, dresses used as social comparison, staff and a forest house; the monograph says the source supplies no wardrobe inventory, domestic routine, private leisure, friendship network or family biography. Not D: no recurring ordinary pattern outside the business arc.

Directed conduct per interlocutor within the arc: Darkness (class comparison, economic regulation, personal provocation, reciprocated by Darkness's own insults and threat); Kazuma as valued hire, then attacked through his party's prestige after the poor result; Aqua's demand answered by a representative apology; Megumin's intervention; guards with their own fear and duty. KD-R01 states what switches courtesy to comparison. Not B: all relationships are sampled inside one arc, and the monograph rejects any demonstrated attraction to Kazuma. Not D: the switch between interlocutors and states is analysed with locators.

Her states are reached only through Kazuma's observations (an unsmiling-eyed smile, a table strike, teeth grinding, tears, pallor) and others' interpretations; the monograph says these support changes in publicly enacted affect, not a diagnosis or proof that every smile is calculated, and treats Megumin's explanation of her embarrassment as interpretation. Not D: no private state is analysed beyond enacted affect.

KD-R03 is supported by repeated within-arc switches: legal-status objection and near tears when Darkness's threat becomes immediate (P225-P228), renewed menace after rescue (P453-P477), invocation of guards and a claimed high level (P496-P505), fear (P510), and a bounty threat retracted at Kazuma's extended hand (P515-P517); her local threat management repeatedly fails. Not B: the model itself rates the mechanism's distinctiveness beyond generic fear as weak and no threshold is identifiable. Not D: the recovery branch and the inhibition branch are each located and given falsifiers.

Her stated justifications are located (willing borrowers agreed to high interest and forceful collection, P222; the dangerous summoning item as a source of money, P476) beside exceptions that defeat an exploitation-only reading (representative apology at P54, actual contractual payment at P235). Not C: no weighing is shown and the closing apology is elicited by fear without accepted responsibility. Not E: positions recur across two commercial domains and are conditioned by KD-R02.

The items analyse the comedy built around her (competing evaluations, guards on the wrong side of bars, reversed threats), not any play of her own; her mockery of the one-kill report is analysed as contempt. Nothing is established about her humour.

The whole known arc is covered with paragraph locators and an explicit separation of direct action, represented speech, attributed report and inference; both items are active_provisional, the MASK name join is open, and the monograph lists political and family history, exact accounts, combat capacity, legal outcome and later response to noncoercive correction as open work. Not C: the subject's evidence is one connected arc with no ordinary life outside it. Not E: that arc is analysed in full by dedicated items.

Located limits and countercases: actual payment and a representative apology defeat a total refusal-of-obligation account; renewed threat after fear defeats a permanent-submission rule; her high-level claim produces no performed spell or successful delay; P213 does not establish that she knew of Kazuma's death; two thefts were completed and the third stopped; no hidden attraction to Kazuma is established; no verdict or punishment is narrated. Not B: these limits are confined to one arc. Not D: they are evidenced, not inferred from silence.

The sequence is ordered by paragraph and the earlier rescue is placed before the later episode, with within-episode state changes located; there is no dating and no longer chronology. Not C: no period conditions beyond the arc's internal order. Not E: the ordering and its limit are explicit.

conditions: Illustrative short written-Japanese lines only, never presented as quotation, in the sampled acts: formal self-presentation, elaborate praise of a valued hire, cutting comparison toward a rival, money-centred justification, command, alarm and abrupt placation.
Vary the act by recipient and situation; do not repeat one source insult or a noble-lady catchphrase, and do not make every line a stammer.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Within or immediately after the U021 episode, with Karen holding only what she knows there (not Kazuma's death at P213, not the reader's causal assembly of her business).
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: A hired adventurer of Kazuma's party's standing, a status rival of Darkness's kind, or her own staff and guards; MASK Karen's relationships are excluded.
setting_constraints: An Axel-area noble household or business transaction in canonical-comic mode, with actual magic and class hierarchy.
Transfer mode only with its own assets, risks and institutions: no imported aristocratic impunity, magic, high level, addiction or diagnostic labels.
No ordinary-life, family or romance content.

scenario_readiness.note: KD-R01 to KD-R03 support narrow prediction of stance in a comparable situation when her knowledge, believed protection and stakes are supplied. Not READY: motive weights are unfixed, transfer to unfamiliar domains is rated low by the model, and the rules come from one arc. Not NOT_READY: each rule is conditioned and falsifiable.
The monograph records no domestic routine, leisure, friendship network or family biography outside the connected house and business arc; receptions are business acts.
Only justifications and their exceptions are located; no weighing of obligations is shown, and the final apology is elicited by fear without accepted responsibility.

The items affirmatively reject a demonstrated attraction or binding romance with Kazuma: her hand-taking praise is selective evaluation of a hire, and no hidden attraction is necessary or established.

conditions: Her role as Donnelly head arranging paid work and defending endorsed practices under KD-R02, with the representative-apology and payment exceptions retained.
No exact wealth, probabilities, returns, legal judgement or institutional consequence beyond her own claims.
scenario_readiness.note: Hiring, contract, payment and commercial justification are her best-sampled conduct. Not READY: no accounts, profit arithmetic or legal outcome is evidenced. Not NOT_READY: arranging work, flattering a sought specialist, paying for completed work and defending her lending and summoning business are located.

known_limits.statement: The reported MASK adventurer Karen is not joined to this subject; a shared first name is insufficient for merger, and the absence of a bridge does not prove the two are distinct.
All evidence comes from one connected arc; her repeated changes within it are not independent lifetime samples.
The global weights of commercial return, standing, useful service, household position and immediate safety are not fixed, so which motive decides a new choice is undetermined.
Generic hostile-noble convention, genre pacing, ordinary fear, social comparison and business incentives all explain part of the same material, and no independent observation separates them.
The model reports no independent prediction result; no exact case or first response had been serialized at its boundary, and a plausible output would not validate it.
Darkness's explanation at P213 is interrupted, so Karen is not shown to know of Kazuma's death when she mocks the one-kill report; a knowing mockery would be invention.
Her high-level-noble claim, guards and summoning stones give no demonstrated control: no spell is performed, the guards are separated by bars, and two stones are taken before use.

The two completed clothing thefts violate her bodily agency; the third attempt is stopped. No third theft, completed exposure or justified coercive method may be supplied, and the violation is not a testing method.
No domestic routine, leisure, friendships, family biography, exact commercial accounts, combat capacity, legal outcome or later response to noncoercive correction is evidenced.
Voice evidence is written Japanese only, without audio, accent or native-human validation.
